name: Arm Scalable Vector Extension
description: Arm designed a vector instruction set extension for AArch64 in which processors can implement vector lengths from 128 to 2,048 bits in 128-bit steps. The design allows vector-length-agnostic software to run across those choices without recompilation. Per-lane predicates control which elements take part in an operation.

date.basis: The dated Arm presentation title slide gives the day and venue.

events.statement: Arm presented SVE for its 64-bit Armv8-A architecture at Hot Chips 28 in Cupertino, California.

evidence.supports: Dates the public presentation and describes the vector instruction architecture.
Explains implementation-selected vector length, predication and the vector-length-agnostic model.

earliest_record.rationale: The dated designer presentation documents the extension. It does not establish when the specification was first drafted or when working silicon first existed.

research.note: The extension was initially presented for high-performance computing. Arm's account links its design to wider vectors and compiler vectorization for those workloads.

links.statement: Arm designed SVE for the AArch64 execution state and allocated SVE instructions within the existing A64 encoding space.
links.scope: The base architecture for the SVE instruction encoding.

evidence.supports: Defines A64 as the fixed-width instruction set of AArch64 before the SVE extension.
Arm's ISA architect explicitly places SVE in AArch64 and identifies its share of the A64 encoding space.
Independent university researchers build with the Armv8.2-A plus SVE target and execute SVE instructions on A64FX hardware.
